newsitem.title: USA: SRP sees agreement on Mexico power transmission.
newsitem.headline: SRP sees agreement on Mexico power transmission.

text.p: The Salt River Project (SRP) expects to reach agreement with El Paso Electric Co, possibly by the end of the day, on access to power transmission lines into northern Mexico, SRP said Wednesday.
SRP, a state-operated power agency based in Phoenix, Ariz., was the lowest bidder in a solicitation by Comision Federal de Electricidad (CFE) to supply 200 megawatts for calendar 1997.

CFE, Mexico's national utility, currently receives the power from El Paso, which has claimed that it does not have enough extra transmission capcity to carry electricity from Arizona to its interconnect with Mexico.
"We are willing to cut El Paso into the deal," said Lisa Urias, head of SRP's Mexican power group.
She was unable to comment on SRP's bid, but said it was "substantially below" El Paso's contract price of around $45.00 per megawatt hour.
"They will be receiving U.S. market prices," Urias noted.
SRP does not have any other long-term contracts with Mexico, but is aggressively pursuing potential opportunities, she said.
"This is a wonderful first step in our hopes of pursuing the Mexican market," Urias said.
